chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu Ayyub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

When you see the crescent, fast; and when you see it, break your fast. It is not by opinion nor by conjecture, but by actual sighting. And the sighting is not that ten people stand and look, one says 'It is there,' and the other nine do not see it; if one sees it, all ten see it. And if there is an impediment, complete the month of Sha'ban as thirty [days]. And Hammad added in it: 'And it is not that one man says 'It is there,' 'I do not know,' except that he says, 'And not fifty.'
ai.seo_question: What are the Shia jurisprudential criteria for sighting the crescent to begin fasting in Ramadan?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the principle of 'ru'yah' (visual sighting) as the definitive criterion for Ramadan, explicitly rejecting 'al-ra'y' (independent reasoning) and 'al-tazanniy' (conjecture) to ensure communal unity. It clarifies that the testimony of a single just witness is sufficient for the entire community to fast, reflecting the Shia emphasis on accessible, evidence-based religious observance rather than complex astronomical calculations. The ruling to complete thirty days of Sha'ban in case of impediment (such as cloudy skies) underscores the practical application of these rules in maintaining the lunar calendar's integrity.
